title: Containment Is Lying to You: Measuring AI Agents Like Employees — Druid AI
talk_summary: Druid AI presents a 26-component, 6-pillar scorecard for evaluating AI agents, weighted toward business governance (39%) over technical metrics, scored 0/1/2 (missing/measurable/managed). Their core claim is that single vanity metrics like containment mislead, and agents should be re-scored weekly against a human baseline to catch drift.

takeaways.technique: Multi-component weighted agent scorecard with 0/1/2 maturity levels
takeaways.what_they_do: Score each agent on ~26 components across mandate, platform, runtime, output, governance; each component gets 0 (missing), 1 (measurable), 2 (managed/tracked over time), then weight by importance.
takeaways.numbers: 26 components; governance weighted 39%, mandate 26%, platform 12%, outputs 9%

takeaways.technique: Success criteria defined at task creation, not after
takeaways.what_they_do: Require every task to carry explicit success criteria written when the task is created, so output can be judged later; without it you cannot tell if the run succeeded.
takeaways.evidence_quote: How do I know it's the success criteria created together with the task? Because if I look and I see that the agent renewed the contract, I want to measure if that renewal was successful

takeaways.what_they_do: Define exactly which systems and endpoints each agent may touch, and who may invoke it, rather than granting broad MCP access.

takeaways.technique: Per-agent budget as a scored mandate item
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat staying within a defined budget as part of the agent's mandate and score it, so cost overruns are caught as a governance failure, not a surprise invoice.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I want to stay in the budget. I don't want to have the surprise that one week later, my agent consumed 20K

takeaways.technique: Weekly re-scoring against human baseline to detect drift
takeaways.what_they_do: Re-run the same evaluation weekly on live traffic against a human baseline; a flat vanity dashboard can hide a score sliding from 83 to 60.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The teal line is the wheel score sliding from 83 to 60 because you're measuring it on a weekly basis
takeaways.numbers: Score drifted 83→60 while dashboard stayed flat at 92%

takeaways.what_they_do: Route all agent-to-human or agent-to-agent handoffs through one central action center instead of each agent implementing its own handoff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I don't want each agent to handle his own handoff. I want to have a central action center where people are engaging with all agents
